along with building therein came to be acquired for the implementation of Bengaluru Metro Rail Project.

The SLAO on finding that the market value recommended by PSS Thomas Committee was fair and reasonable, passed general award on 05/11/2008 fixing the market value of land at Rs. 37,862/- per Sq.Mtr and the structure compensation at Rs. 4,26,099/- and totally awarded Rs.
31,91,492/-.

The possession of the acquired property was taken on 04/12/2008.
.7.
Under Section 18(3) (a) of LA Act, the SLAO had to send the reference within 90 days from the date of receipt of the application under Sub-section (1) of Section 18 to the reference court.
The SLAO did not do so.
He made the reference after the expiry of 90 days from the date of receipt of the said application.
Hence the present reference is bad.
The application filed U.s, 18 in the present case is bald.
Without laying the foundation in the application, the applicant cannot adduce evidence and in case they adduce evidence, the same cannot be considered by the reference court.

.8. It is stated that the Thomas Committee, after valuation analysis of representative land parcels of different categories and also after considering guideline value and sales statistics recommended for fixing of the market value of the property in question at Rs. 37,862/- per Sq.Mtr.
The said valuation is scientific and in accordance with Section 23 of LA Act.
The SLAO adopted the same value under general ward.
There is no good ground to hold that fixation of market value in the general award is unjust or improper or unacceptable.

It may be that under the award (Exhibit-P15) pertaining to property No. 1487(34) which is an intermediary site situated along Mahakavi Kuvempu Road,
Prakashnagar BBMP ward No. 23, the market value is fixed at Rs. 39,369/- per Sq.mtr.

But in the present case, the Thomas Committee has recommended the market value at Rs.37,862/- per Sq.mtr,
after considering the individual attributes of the property.
The price fetched for a commercial site during auction cannot be made the basis for fixing the market value.
The claimants are not entitled for fixation of market value at Rs. 76,633/- per Sq.mtr as claimed by them.
Hence prayed for rejection of the reference.
9. To prove their case, claimant No.2 M. Subramanyam has been examined as PW.1.

The documents marked at Ex.P.1 to 26.

The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka had allowed the petition and judgment dated 15-07-2022 has been set aside.
The matter is remitted back for reconsideration afresh.

In 2003(2) MLJ 436 our Hon'ble high court has held as follows.

"It is also the equally well settled legal position that the claimants stand in the position of plaintiffs and the burden is on them to prove by adducing cogent and acceptable evidence that the lands are capable of fetching higher market value than what is determined by the land acquisition officer, which is only an offer.
The burden to prove that the amount awarded by the land acquisition officer is not adequate is always on the claimant.

Such burden could be discharged by adducing relevant and material evidence to establish that the acquired lands are capable of fetching higher market value than the amount awarded by the land acquisition officer.
The very object of reference U/s.18 is to bring on record the principles which the land under acquisition was capable of fetching in the open market as on date of the notification."

sentences.text: In this case, the Reference Court and High Court, after referring to the evidence relating to other sale transactions, found them to be inapplicable as they related to far away properties.
Therefore we are left with only the auction sale transactions.

On the facts and circumstances, we are of the view that a deduction or cut of 20% in the auction price disclosed by the relied upon auction transaction towards the factor of `competitive - price hike' would enable us to arrive at the fair market price."
From the above discussion it is clear that auction sale is reliable only when there is no other comparable sales.
The respondent has produced the sale statistics for the year 2005 in respect of properties near the acquired area.
As per sale statistics for the year 2005 the average market value is Rs.880per sq.ft.
There is large difference between the market value for the year 2005 and auction sale.
So I do not intend to rely on auction sale.

The respondent has in their evidence stated that the market value determined and the consent award can be considered for determining the market value of the property in question.
In para No.20 I have held that the acquired land in the present case is the corner site and so the claimant is entitled for additional 10%.
The market value would be Rs.39,369+3963=Rs.43,305.
Thus the claimant is entitled to market value of Rs.43,305/- per sq.mtr.
